Research Question

Research Question Does neighbourhood drive up sale prices in the central area of Ames, Iowa or are other factors more influential at determining sale price?

Sub questions: 1) Is the relationship between quality / condition and price negligible or significant?

  1. Does the period of remodelling and original construction heave great significance on sale price?

  2. To what extent do structural characteristics play a prominent role in determining sale price in Iowa (e.g. house style and area)?

Research Focus Our focus for researching this particular dataset is to determine the strength of a correlation between the response variable of house sale price, and various explanatory variables including but not limited to house style, area and period of remodelling.

Data

Include a citation for your data. See http://libraryguides.vu.edu.au/c.php?g=386501&p=4347840 for guidance on proper citation for datasets. If you got your data off the web, make sure to state the retrieval date.

Data description Our analysis explores the House prices data (collected between 2006 and 2010) which is a dataset, accessed on 30/10/26, consisting of 82 variables and 2930 observations. These variables include the prices of houses sold in Iowa along with their various features, such as basement quality, in addition to structural characteristics stories and overall quality, across different residential areas. The vast spread of data is highly beneficial for providing us with insight into both qualitative and quantitative factors in influencing house prices in Iowa during this period. Thus, enabling us to scale down the data into fewer of both qualitative and quantitative variables (with respect to our question).

Methodology Initially, it was determined most vital to clean the dataset. Our first step for this was to narrow down the location into just the central area using the filter function. We took effort to avoid removing columns unnecessarily as to avoid a bias in our results which would present if other variables i.e. basement quality were deceivingly insignificant. Thereby, as we had not fully confirmed out question, and subsequently concluded our reading on the area of focus, we chose to keep the columns as originally presented. Though, as recommended by the data publishers we did remove a row including an outlier to minimise the possibility of inaccurate interpretations during our initial exploration. The data, in regards to our specific area of focus, did not require extensive cleaning, rather our tidying involved mutating the overwhelmingly large data into smaller specific columns which would allow us to easily interpret the information and allow for efficient comparisons. For example, we transformed the “year built” into general periods i.e. Interwar. As a result, this enabled us to form our research question of: “Does neighbourhood drive up sale prices in the central area of Ames, Iowa or are other factors more influential in dtermining sale price?”, our chosen approach was to divide this broad question into three sub questions: 1) Is the relationship between quality / condition and price negligible or significant? 2) Does the period of remodelling and orginal construction heave great significance on sale price? 3) What is the role of structural characteristics in determining sale price in Iowa (ie house style - stories, area etc.)? Creating relevant visualisations for these sub questions was crucial in our analysis as it not only strengthened our initial understanding of these variables, but reinforced the dominant ideas displayed across these visualisations. For example, we were able to hypothesise from our these visualisations that size is not necessarily the most influential factor in influencing prices of houses sold in Iowa during this time.

Findings

Initial Exploration & Findings

We stared with visual analyses of how the Prices of Houses in Amez are affected by different factors:

Graph 1) Price of houses by Era Built: The median/ average of victorian & gilded age is the lowest which means the average prices of houses in the Victorian and Gilded age is lower than any other Era but only marginally in comparison to interwar and post war but more prominently in comparison to 20th century & modern. Victorian & gilded age have more significant extreme price variety, while post war has least extreme price variety, 20th century & modern has overall highest average, average across all eras is less than/ equal to $200,000, 20th century & modern has no extremes.

Graph 2) Prices of houses by Era Remodelled: We can see an increasing relationship as median price increases as move closer to recent remodelling. The 1980s&1990s and 2000s have no lower extremes, but high ones (1980s and 1990s has highest extreme).

Graph 3 and 4) House Prices by Area(Square Feet): The graph shows a positive relationship between house area and sale price, although the considerable spread around the line of best fit suggests that area is not the sole determinant of price. Houses with fewer stories tend to cluster below the line, while some houses with more stories achieve higher prices despite having similar floor areas.

  1. House Price by Quality of Build and Condition of Maintenance Graphs: There is a clear positive correlation between a house’s overall quality rating and its selling price. Properties rated between 3 and 6 (out of 10) have relatively similar median prices and data distributions. However, those rated above 7 generally sell for considerably more. Houses rated 10 sold for $475,000, compared with just $12,000 for those rated 2. The relationship is less apparent when considering the house’s overall condition at the time of sale. Median selling prices remain relatively similar across all condition ratings, while the interquartile ranges are considerably wider.

  1. Residuals plot graph: The graph shows that the model of house prices versus area does have a relatively linear relationship.   1. House Prices By quality by neighbourhood graph: A clear relationship is exemplified in this graph as two houses in the same neighbourhood of Old Town, with different ratings are sold for very different prices. However, the hypothesis can still be supported by the evidence within the medium ratings as Crawford and college creek continue to show higher prices than other neighbourhoods where houses had the same quality rating, yet this trend is less clear than the overall correlation between quality and price.

Linear regression model

A multiple linear regression model has been selected as we aim to analyse both categorical and continuous variables and their inferential relationships. The Positive coefficient of the area estimate suggests that house prices on average are higher for houses with a larger area. Since the P-value for area is very small, this suggests a statistically significant result and that the area is an influential variable on house prices. Birkside has been set as the reference neighbourhood. The large positive coefficients for college creek and Crawford neighbourhoods suggests they have a significantly higher predicted house prices holding area and quality constant. This reinforces the previous claims that these neighbourhoods drive up prices regardless of other factors. However, the other neighbourhoods have higher p-values and coefficients with lower magnitudes, suggesting less statistically significant results. So, for other neighbourhoods in the central area, area and quality are likely more significant. All of the quality coefficients are large and positive, clearly showing that price increases as quality rating improves. The smaller p-values as quality rises suggests increasing statistical significance holding area and neighbourhood constant, reinforcing the highly influential nature of quality in determining house prices.

linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(price_k ~ area + Neighborhood + Overall.Qual, data = central_data_with_eras) %>%
  tidy()

Prices of Houses with Repect to Basement Size:

Another possible explanatory variable could be the size of the basement. There is a positive correlation shown through this visualisation however, this should be considered alongside total area of the house and therefore is likley not a highly influential variable.

The initial findings suggest that neighbourhood has a considerable influence on house sale prices in Ames, although it is not the only determining factor. Crawford has the highest average sale price, while Old Town has the lowest. College Creek also appears to command relatively higher prices compared with neighbourhoods such as Edwards and Brookside. However, the considerable variation in prices within individual neighbourhoods suggests that other characteristics also contribute to property values.

Findings for sub question 1 “Is the relationship between quality / condition and price negligible or significant?” present that the overall build quality has a strong positive relationship with house sale prices. As the overall quality rating increases, the median sale price also rises. This suggests that buyers place substantial value on properties with better construction and finishing standards. In comparison, overall condition appears to have a weaker relationship with sale price. Therefore build quality appears to be a more influential factor than general property condition when determining sale price.

Findings for sub question 2 “Does the period of remodelling and original construction heave great significance on sale price?” present that the original construction demonstrates some variation in sale prices. Victorian and Gilded Age properties have the lowest median prices, although their values are only marginally below those of Interwar and Post-war properties. In contrast, 20th-century and modern properties generally achieve higher median sale prices. Victorian and Gilded Age houses also display greater price variation, suggesting that older properties can still achieve considerably different market values. The period of remodelling demonstrates a clearer positive relationship with sale price. Properties remodelled more recently tend to have higher median prices, with houses remodelled during the 1980s, 1990s and 2000s generally achieving higher values than those remodelled in earlier periods. This suggests that modernisation and property improvements may contribute to increased market value.

Findings for sub question 3 “To what extent do structural characteristics play a prominent role in determining sale price in Iowa (e.g. house style and area)” presents that structural characteristics, particularly house area, play an important role in determining sale prices. There is a clear positive relationship with between the total living area (square feet) and sale price, indicating that larger properties generally achieve higher market values. However, the considerable spread of observations around the line of best fit suggests that house size alone cannot fully explain differences in property prices. The number of stories also contributes to varying sale prices. Properties with fewer storeys tend to cluster below the line of best fit, whereas some houses with more storeys achieve higher prices despite having similar floor areas. From this we can conclude that comparisons across neighbourhoods suggests that similarly sized houses can achieve different prices depending on their location.

Ethical Considerations

“There are 5 observations that an instructor may wish to remove from the data set before giving it to students (a plot of SALE PRICE versus GR LIV AREA will indicate them quickly). Three of them are true outliers (Partial Sales that likely don’t represent actual market values) and two of them are simply unusual sales (very large houses priced relatively appropriately). I would recommend removing any houses with more than 4000 square feet from the data set (which eliminates these 5 unusual observations) before assigning it to students.”

Final Conclusion

To conclude, from our extensive analysis across various neighbourhoods, we can detrmine that overall quality can be considered the largest factor in influencing prices of houses sold in central Ames, Iowa between 2006-2010. Thus, subsequently, quality is likely to be a prominent determinant when predicting which houses will receive a higher selling price. Interestingly, our inital hypothesis of believing neighbourhood played a signifcant role in driving up sale prices is not entirely to be neglected or discarded, as within 2 dominant neighbourhoods: College Creek and Crawford, the selling prices were notably larger than that of other neighbourhoods when holding quality and house area roughly equal. In turn, suggesting that for these 2 specific neighbourhoods the location itself forces a higher selling price irrespective of quality, area, period of remodel and period built. Our visualisations and models support this general conclusion as “Prices buyers pay per sq ft area” demonstrates that houses in Crawford and College Creek buyers pay more in these locations for the same square footage of area. In addition, the positive relationship between overall quality and selling price as found in “House Price by Quality of Build and Condition of Maintenance Graphs” suggests that a property’s condition at the time of sale has limited influence on its selling price. When considering both factors together, a positive linear relationship is evident between overall quality and selling price. However, condition continues to have only a marginal effect on either the quality rating or the price. This suggests that a property’s condition at the time of sale has limited influence on its selling price. When considering both factors together, a positive linear relationship is evident between overall quality and selling price. This reflects a clear relationship between quality and price of houses regardless of neighbourhood, suggesting potentially that quality rating is a more influential factor in determining prices. However, there is some evidence that continues to support the hypothesis that neighbourhood is highly influential due to the fact that evidence within the medium ratings of the “House Prices by Quality by Neighbourhood graphs“ confirm the idea that certain neighbourhoods like Crawford and college creek continue to show higher prices than other neighbourhoods despite identical individual house quality rating. Although, this trend between neighbourhood and price irrespective of quality is less evident than the general link between quality and selling price. Furthermore, the results from the linear regression model suggest that property size and quality are important predictors of house prices, while the influence of neighbourhood varies depending on location. House area has a positive relationship with price, while higher quality properties generally achieve higher sale prices. Therefore, although neighbourhood contributes to differences in property values, structural characteristics and property quality are also important determinants. The period of remodelling demonstrates an obvious but not exaggerated or particularly noteworthy relationship with sale price. Additionally, basement size is a valuable factor to consider as it appears those houses with larger basements (sq feet) are more expensive, this must be considered with caution though as this will likely to contribute to overall size (area), the factor discussed in detail above.
